title: Unified Reserve API, Tenant Fallback, and QoS Profiles (PRD)
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Problem statement:
Many tenants using Dedicated experience unpredictable headroom during bursts and on transient demand spikes. Existing reserved pool primitives are split across UI, scheduler, and billing layers with inconsistent semantics for partial preemption and burst fallback. This makes it hard for platform customers to define a single contract that guarantees baseline throughput, safe burst behavior, and predictable cost tradeoffs.

Goal:
Deliver a single, versioned Reserve API and associated QoS profile primitives that let tenants: 1) declare and modify reserved capacity and preferred burst semantics; 2) attach a fallback policy that automatically routes excess traffic to compatible model variants or shared fallback pools; and 3) choose a QoS profile that determines fairness, preemption windows, and grace time. The API should be declarative, observable, and backward compatible with current reserved-pool UI flows.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in customer outage incidents caused by insufficient burst headroom by 60% within 3 months of rollout.
- 40% fewer manual on-call interventions for eviction-related surprises.
- Customers can create/modify reserves via API in <= 2s p95.
- Telemetry dashboards show correct accounting of reserved vs. burst usage per tenant within 1 minute.

Scope (In):
- A versioned REST/SDK Reserve API (v1) with endpoints to create/modify/release reservations and read status.
- QoS profiles baked into reservation objects (profiles: guaranteed, elastic, best-effort, preemptible-with-grace).
- Tenant fallback policy attachments: on-deny and on-evict actions (route to fallback pool, degrade model size, or reject).
- Backend scheduler hooks: acceptance handshake, soft-evict timelines, and preemption grace window enforcement.
- Console UI hooks (read-only) and audit logs for all reservation lifecycle events.
- Telemetry and SLOs: reserve request latency, reserve fulfillment latency, eviction frequency, fallback activation rates.

Scope (Out):
- Billing changes for reserved vs. burst usage (handled by separate billing project).
- New dedicated scheduler rewrite — we will add hooks to the existing scheduler only.
- Non-Dedicated (hosted/shared) customers — this is dedicated-only for initial rollout.

Key user journeys:
1) Establish reserve: Tenant calls POST /reserves with desired vGPU units, duration window, QoS profile, and optional fallback policy. System validates, reserves capacity (or places request in pending if not immediately available), and returns a reservation_id and state.
2) Burst occurs: Incoming requests exceeding reserved capacity trigger the scheduler to consult the reservation object; if fallback policy == route_to_fallback, requests are routed to a configured fallback pool with transparent retry headers. If fallback policy == degrade_model, scheduler substitutes a compatible smaller model.
3) Preemption: When capacity reclamation required, tenants with preemptible-with-grace QoS will receive a soft-evict notification webhook and have the configured grace period to drain active sessions before forced termination.

API contract highlights (examples):
- POST /api/v1/reserves { tenant_id, vgpu_units, window_start, window_end, qos_profile, fallback_policy, metadata } -> 201 { reservation_id, state }
- PATCH /api/v1/reserves/:id { vgpu_delta, qos_profile, fallback_policy } -> 200 { reservation_id, state }
- GET /api/v1/reserves/:id -> 200 { reservation_id, state, usage_metrics }
- Webhook subscription: reservation.soft_evict and reservation.state_change events.

Observability & SLOs:
- Telemetry emitted at every state transition with tags: reservation_id, tenant_id, pool_id, qos_profile, fallback_reason.
- Dashboard templates for: per-tenant reservation utilization, fallback activations, preemption incidents, and p95 reservation latency.
- Alerting: if fallback activation rate > 5% for a tenant over 15m, create a paging alert to SE and account owner.

Privacy/Security considerations:
- All reserve objects are tenant-scoped and visible only to authorized principals per RBAC.
- Audit log entries must be immutable and include caller identity, timestamps, and previous state.
- Because reservation lifecycle can affect routing, a security review is required to ensure no cross-tenant leakage via fallback pools.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha (internal seat): implement API v1 with no public console UI, limited to 5 internal tenants for 2 weeks.
- Beta (select customers): enable for three existing Dedicated customers who opt in; monitor fallback activations and eviction churn for 6 weeks.
- GA: broad availability after fixes and runbook validation.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Fallback pools may become overloaded and amplify failures. Mitigation: rate-limited admission to fallback pools and automatic backpressure signaling to callers.
- Risk: Incorrect QoS mapping causes noisy neighbor preemptions. Mitigation: conservative defaults (guaranteed for P0; elastic for P1), and operator override tooling.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Priya Srinivasan (assignee), Marco Alvarez (creator)
- Eng leads: Runtime (Eng: Kenta Mori), Scheduler (Eng: Leena Gupta), Console (Eng: Omar Reyes)
- Security: Tanya Holt
- Solutions/customer success: Javier Morales

Documentation and artifacts to deliver:
- API spec (OpenAPI) and SDK stubs
- PRD summary and rollout checklist (this doc)
- Runbook for fallback incidents and preemption handling
- Telemetry dashboards and alert definitions

Acceptance criteria are enumerated below. Once these are green, we mark this ticket Done and create follow-ups for billing integration and broader Console write flows.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST/PATCH/GET for /api/v1/reserves implemented and documented in OpenAPI with example payloads
API performance: p95 reserve create/modify requests <= 2s under normal load
Scheduler: QoS profiles respected under simulated contention tests (bench harness with mixed tenants) and preemption grace windows enforced
Fallback: fallback policies (route_to_fallback, degrade_model, reject) execute and are observable; fallback activation emits a telemetry event with reason tags
Observability: dashboard templates available and show correct reserved vs. burst usage within 1 minute of event
Security: RBAC enforcement confirmed in audit logs; security review signed off
Runbook: Incident runbook for runaway fallback pool and preemption paging is authored and reviewed
Rollout: Alpha and Beta sign-ups completed and at least one Beta tenant reports successful failover exercise
Documentation: SDK examples added to README and Console read-only hooks surface reservation state
notes: Decision: use existing scheduler extension points rather than a full rewrite to reduce risk and accelerate delivery.
Trade-off: initial implementation will not change billing model; usage accounting is recorded but billing product will consume it later.
Follow-up (post-GA): integrate reserve visibility into billing UI and add console-based create/modify flows for admins.
